description: SimBench is a dataset of electrical power system benchmark models with grid data from low voltage to extra-high voltage and full-year load, generation and storage profiles, created to support research in grid planning and operation and to make methods reproducible and comparable without relying on real network data that are not publicly available. It came from a research project run from November 2015 to April 2019 under the German Federal Government's 6th Energy Research Programme by the University of Kassel, Fraunhofer IEE, RWTH Aachen University and TU Dortmund, advised by six German distribution network operators; the follow-up SimBench-Sector extends benchmarks to gas and heating networks and coupled applications. Coverage: the grids are designed benchmark networks for all voltage levels with data for cross-level interconnection, developed with German operators, not the network of any real place. Data are distributed through simbench.net and a Python package on PyPI (version 1.6.3, 22 September 2026, Python 3.11 or newer) with documentation that loads grids and profiles into pandapower, and a converter to CSV. The database is published under the Open Database Licence 1.0 at no cost. Caveats: the grids suit method comparison and reproducibility, not studies of a specific location, and parts of the project website are in German only. Simulation uses are network flow, planning and operation studies and benchmarking of optimisation methods. Related records: it is designed for use with model-pandapower and relates to model-pandapipes for the gas and heat benchmarks.
